avoids loading its ~3 MB table for the common case of ASCII slugs.

Raise for negative slice sizes in sliced()

sliced(seq, n) with a negative n silently produced a wrong result
instead of raising or returning empty. Because the internal generator
uses seq[i : i + n] with i stepping by count(0, n), a negative n makes
takewhile(len, ...) yield a single truncated slice and stop:

    >>> list(sliced('ABCDEFG', -1))
    ['ABCDEF']

This is the worst failure mode: no error, just quietly incorrect
output. The documented sibling chunked() already rejects a negative n
(via islice), and tail() was recently changed to raise for negative
sizes for the same reason. sliced() is actually worse than pre-fix
tail(), which returned an empty result rather than wrong data.

Guard n < 0 up front and raise ValueError('n must be at least 0'),
matching tail()'s message. n == 0 still returns an empty iterator
(unchanged), as do all n >= 1 cases. With strict=True the negative
case previously raised a misleading "seq is not divisible by n"; it
now raises the correct domain error before iteration begins.
